title: footgun: normalizeRef appears to normalize a 'self.'-prefixed ref, sitting alongside the 'global.'->'globals.' rewrite as if it transforms the string.
detail: 'self.'.length is 5, so `self.${ref.slice(5)}` strips 'self.' and re-prepends the identical 'self.' — the branch is a pure no-op returning ref unchanged. The 'globals.' branch on line 31 is likewise a no-op. Only the 'global.'->'globals.' branch (line 30) actually rewrites anything.

title: footgun: The entity facade's get trap intercepts prop === 'assignment' to derive { parentId } from the assignmentMap, reading as a convenience accessor added on top of the entity.
detail: RuntimeEntity is Record<string, unknown>, so an entity may carry its own real 'assignment' field; the Proxy unconditionally shadows it and always returns the synthesized { parentId }, so any genuine entity.assignment data is unreachable through the facade.

title: footgun: registerOperations is invoked from the JsonLogicAdapter constructor (JsonLogicAdapter.ts:16), reading as per-instance operation registration.
detail: A module-level `opsRegistered` flag (ops.ts:7) makes every call after the first a no-op, and json-logic-js.add_operation mutates the shared singleton import — so QUERY/QUERY_COUNT/SLOT/SUM are registered exactly once and leak globally into every json-logic-js consumer in the process, not scoped to any adapter instance.

title: Compiler ignores operator precedence; mixed arithmetic/boolean folds strictly left-to-right
detail: The token loop applies every op/keyword in source order with no precedence, so `1 + 2 * 3` compiles to *(+(1,2),3)=9 not 7, and `a AND b OR c` compiles to or(and(a,b),c) regardless of intended grouping. Any rule authored assuming standard precedence silently evaluates to the wrong number/boolean.

title: Tier-2 isolation is enforced on QUERY/SLOT but not on by-id entity access
detail: createLogicDataFacade resolves any unknown top-level var name as an entity id via snapshot.getEntity in ALL modes. json-logic's `var` walks the first path segment, so tier2_entity logic — explicitly blocked from QUERY/QUERY_COUNT (ops.ts:19,33) — can still read arbitrary entities and their fields with `{var:"<entityId>.<field>"}`, defeating the intended tier-2 sandbox.

title: Operator right-hand operand cannot be NOT or a sub-expression
detail: For an `op` token the RHS is read with tokenToAtom(requireToken(index)) rather than consumeAtom(), so `x == NOT y` throws LogicCompileError('Unexpected token keyword') even though NOT is accepted as an AND/OR operand and at expression start. The grammar is asymmetric and rejects otherwise-reasonable comparisons against a negated value.

title: Shared EMPTY_SELF singleton used as default self target
detail: A single module-level EMPTY_SELF = {} is reused as the Proxy target for every evaluation whose context.self is nullish. The facade is read-only today so this is benign, but any future write through the self facade (or a json-logic op mutating `this`) would leak state across unrelated evaluations. It also has no id, so assignmentMap lookups collapse to assignmentMap[''].

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: QUERY returns [] when __snapshot is absent OR tag is not a string. A malformed tag (number/undefined) is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty query result, so a typo'd or wrong-typed tag silently evaluates as 'no matching entities' rather than erroring — real: can mask authoring mistakes in rules.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: QUERY_COUNT returns 0 when __snapshot is absent OR tag is not a string, conflating a malformed/wrong-typed tag with a legitimate count of zero; a rule gated on QUERY_COUNT(badTag) > 0 silently never fires. Real for rule correctness, benign for crash-safety.

title: silent failure: ignored-return
detail: SLOT returns [] when slotName is not a string (and [] for a missing slot), so a mistyped slot reference yields an empty entity list instead of an error. Combined with SUM (which returns 0 for non-arrays), a broken SLOT path silently produces 0 downstream. Real: masks slot-name authoring errors.
